content:
The get_template returned a dict as a string with single quotes. It includes retro_smarts_template and canonical_smarts_template. The retro_smarts_template seems to have two reactants on left side: '[NH2;D1;+0:5]-[c:6].[O;D1;H0:7]=[C:8]-[c;H0;D3;+0:9]1:[cH;D2;+0:1]:[c:2]:[c:3]:[cH;D2;+0:4]:[c;H0;D3;+0:10]:1-[C:11]=[O;D1;H0:12]>>...' So the template expects two reactants: an amine (NH2 attached to aromatic) and a carboxylic acid (or activated). Our target molecule is a large sulfonyl aryl with an amide attached to an aniline? Let's examine target: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

It contains an amide: C(=O)N attached to an aniline (c3ccccc3N). The amide nitrogen is attached to aromatic amine (aniline). The template likely breaks amide bond to give amine and carboxylic acid. So precursors: the amine part (aniline) and the carboxylic acid part (the rest). The amine part is the aromatic amine: Nc3ccccc3 (maybe with H). The carboxylic acid part is the rest: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O) )cc2)cc1? Actually the amide carbonyl attached to the aromatic amine: /C=C/C(=O)N-... So the acid part is the fragment containing the carbonyl and the rest of molecule: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O) )cc2)cc1 plus the carbonyl carbon attached to the double bond? The acid would be the aliphatic carboxylic acid: /C=C/C(=O)OH? But our target has N attached, not OH. So the precursor acid is the same but with OH instead of N. So we need to replace N with OH.

Thus precursors likely: 1) the amine: Nc3ccccc3 (maybe as aniline: c1ccc(N)cc1? Actually the amine is attached to the carbonyl carbon, not aromatic? Wait the amide is C(=O)N c3ccccc3N? Actually SMILES: ...C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N. So carbonyl attached to N which is attached to phenyl with an NH2 substituent (an aniline). So the amine precursor is an aniline with NH2: c3ccccc3N (aniline). The acid precursor is the rest: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2)cc1? plus the double bond? Actually the acid would be the same chain but with OH at carbonyl: .../C=C/C(=O)O. So the acid SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2)cc1

Thus we propose two precursors: ['Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2)cc1', 'c1ccccc1N'] but need correct SMILES for aniline: 'c1ccccc1N' (aniline). However the amine in target is attached to carbonyl, not free; but the amine precursor is aniline (c1ccccc1N). That seems plausible.

We should verify using apply_template with this template but maybe need to provide both reactants. The template expects two reactants: amine and acid. So we can output list of list with these two SMILES.

Thus final answer: [['Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2)cc1', 'c1ccccc1N']]

Check if any other possible combos: maybe the amine could be aniline with extra N? Actually the amine part includes the N attached to phenyl and also the phenyl has an NH2 substituent (the same N). The SMILES 'c3ccccc3N' is aniline. So fine.

Return that.
